title: Confidential Information Memorandum – BlueCrest Marine Holdings, Inc. ("Project Driftwood")
summary: BlueCrest Marine Holdings, Inc. is the leading independent manufacturer and distributor of marine hardware and accessories in North America, with $420M LTM revenue and $56M LTM Adj. EBITDA (13.3% margin). Founded in 1978 and headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, FL, the company serves 800+ customers across OEM (65%), specialty retail (29%), and DTC/Amazon (6%) channels, with 2,800+ active SKUs across 14 product categories. The Halverson family (2nd generation ownership) is seeking a sale for liquidity and to pursue institutional-capital-backed growth. Key investment highlights include: #1/#2 market share in 8 of 14 categories, blue-chip OEM relationships averaging 18-year tenure, 22% YoY branded retail growth, significant DTC upside ($35–50M accessible), and $8–12M EBITDA improvement opportunity from ERP/procurement modernization. Revenue CAGR from FY22–LTM is ~7.3%. The process is managed by Baird Industrial & Services, with Phase 1 IOIs due August 2025 and expected close in Q2 2026.

key_quotes.quote: BlueCrest Marine Holdings, Inc. is the leading independent manufacturer and distributor of marine hardware and accessories in North America, with $420M LTM revenue and $56M LTM Adj. EBITDA (13.3% margin).

65% of revenue from OEM agreements with Malibu Boats, MasterCraft, Brunswick, Grady-White, Sea Ray (div. of Brunswick), Chaparral, Boston Whaler (div. of Brunswick), Tracker (div. of Bass Pro), Ranger, and 6 other OEM partners. Average top-5 OEM relationship tenure: 18 years.
LEK market study estimates $35–50M of additional DTC revenue accessible within 18 months with dedicated investment. Margin on DTC is 500bps above retail channel.

Current ERP is a customized QuickBooks installation from 2009. No formal procurement function. Estimated $8–12M EBITDA opportunity from: (a) Oracle NetSuite or SAP implementation, (b) centralized procurement of raw materials (aluminum, stainless steel, marine-grade plastics), (c) pricing optimization through better SKU-level margin visibility.
BlueCrest is being sold to provide liquidity for the Halverson family and capitalize on significant value-creation opportunities that are best pursued with institutional ownership.

growth_drivers: Market leadership in 8 of 14 product categories with pricing power and preferred vendor status
Blue-chip OEM customer base with 18-year average tenure and 3-year contracts
Branded retail channel (BlueCrest Pro Series) growing 22% YoY with 400bps higher gross margin
Secular tailwinds: rising US boat registrations, premiumization, and higher accessories attach rates
Significant untapped DTC opportunity — estimated $35–50M incremental revenue within 18 months
Operational upside of $8–12M EBITDA from ERP implementation, centralized procurement, and pricing optimization
risks: OEM channel concentration — 65% of revenue from boat manufacturers subject to marine industry cyclicality
Top-heavy customer list (Malibu, MasterCraft, Brunswick) creates customer concentration risk
Outdated ERP (customized QuickBooks from 2009) and lack of formal procurement function
CFO is founder's spouse with dual family office responsibilities — management quality / succession concern
Commodity input exposure to aluminum, stainless steel, and marine-grade plastics
CEO is 68 years old with no prior PE experience — founder transition and management continuity risk

title: Project Driftwood — Confidential Teaser (Baird Industrial & Services, July 2025)

The company generates $420M LTM revenue and $56M LTM Adj. EBITDA (13.3% margin), with ~65% of revenue from long-term OEM relationships with top boat builders. title: Project Driftwood — Top 50 Customer Analysis
summary: This workbook provides a ranked analysis of Project Driftwood's top 50 customers by LTM revenue through September 2025, covering both OEM accounts and aftermarket/dealer customers. The top 50 customers span marine OEM manufacturers (outboard, inboard, pontoon, electric/hybrid, commercial/workboat), national and regional dealer networks, government/military contracts, commercial operators (fishing, towing, ferry), and export distributors. The top 2 customers (Marine OEM Client A and Client B) account for $52.4M and $38.6M in LTM revenue respectively, with Client A being a sole-source relationship at 2,800 units/year and Client B under a 3-year fixed-pricing contract through 2027. Top 10 customers collectively represent ~$215.5M of LTM revenue. The customer base reflects a marine propulsion/components manufacturer with a national and international footprint, long-tenured key accounts, and meaningful government contract exposure.

growth_drivers: Fastest-growing OEM segment (pontoon boats, Client D)
Electric/hybrid propulsion pilot program (Client I) growing rapidly
International export expansion (Europe, Australia/NZ, Latin America, Southeast Asia)
Hurricane-replacement aftermarket demand (Gulf Coast)
Growing online/independent parts retail channel (Client EE)
risks: High customer concentration: top 2 OEM clients represent outsized share of LTM revenue ($52.4M and $38.6M)
Sole-source dependency on Client A (primary hull manufacturer, 2,800 units/yr)
Government/military contract exposure with IDIQ and multi-year structures (Clients E, M, Y)
Emerging/pilot OEM relationships with short tenures (Clients I, U, AA) carrying execution risk
Seasonal and cyclical nature of recreational marine aftermarket

title: Project Driftwood — Operations Overview: BlueCrest Marine Holdings, Inc.
summary: IC memorandum covering the operational profile of BlueCrest Marine Holdings, Inc. (Project Driftwood). Details a two-facility manufacturing footprint in Fort Lauderdale, FL (primary, 220k sq ft, 74% utilization, leased below-market from Halverson family LLC) and Tampa, FL (secondary, 95k sq ft, 68% utilization, owned). Products span deck hardware, anchoring/fender systems, marine lighting, and dock hardware. Contract manufacturing accounts for ~52% of COGS across four partners (two domestic, two China-based). Key raw materials include marine-grade stainless steel (24% of COGS, no volume contract), aluminum alloy (18%), marine plastics (12%), and electrical components (8%) — all procured largely on spot terms, representing a meaningful cost-reduction opportunity via volume contracting. Operational KPIs show consistent improvement across FY22–LTM: OEM on-time delivery reached 94.1%, fill rate 97.8%, inventory turns 5.9x, and defect/warranty rate down to 1.1%. Below-market lease ($3.8M vs. ~$5.8M market) is flagged as a post-close normalization item.

key_quotes.quote: Fort Lauderdale facility leased from a Halverson family LLC at below-market rent ($3.8M vs. estimated market rent of $5.8M per CBRE appraisal Q3 2025). Post-close, ACP expects to either acquire the property or renegotiate at market.
No volume contract; spot pricing … $2.5–3.5M via annual contract with 1–2 mills [on marine-grade stainless steel].
On-time delivery to OEMs: 94.1% [LTM]; OEM fill rate: 97.8% [LTM].
Defect / warranty rate: 1.8% [FY22A] … 1.1% [LTM].

growth_drivers: Consistent improvement in OEM on-time delivery and fill rates
Inventory turns improvement from 5.4x to 5.9x over FY22–LTM
Significant procurement savings opportunity ($5.2–7.8M) via volume contracts and hedging on stainless steel, aluminum, and plastics
Manufacturing throughput improvement to 97.5% LTM

~22% of COGS sourced from China-based CM partners, creating tariff and geopolitical supply chain risk

title: Project Driftwood — LBO Model (Base Case)
summary: LBO financial model for Project Driftwood prepared by Atlas Crossing Partners Fund IV in February 2026. The model reflects a June 30, 2026 entry at a $580M enterprise value on $56M LTM Adj. EBITDA (implying a ~10.4x entry multiple). LTM revenue is $420M. The capital structure consists of $320M senior secured TLB (Golub Capital), $110M Atlas Crossing equity, $110M Halverson family rollover (~19%), and $48M management equity pool (8%). The QofE bridge (Deloitte preliminary) reconciles reported EBITDA of $39.4M to $56.6M Adj. EBITDA through add-backs including D&A normalization, excess family compensation, one-time legal/IP costs, and restructuring charges. Base case P&L projections show revenue growing from $420M (LTM) to $604M by FY30B, with EBITDA margins expanding from ~14.5% to ~18.5%. Returns sensitivity runs across downside (exit EV at 8.5x on $68M EBITDA), base (10.5x on $95M), and upside (12x on $120M) scenarios over a 5-year hold. Key growth drivers include OEM and aftermarket/parts revenue growth, with aftermarket mix rising from 38% to 42% of total revenue. Automation capex is a notable investment theme.

growth_drivers: OEM revenue growth (8.5% blended, tapering to 6.5%)
Aftermarket / parts growth (10% tapering to 8%)
Aftermarket mix expansion from 38% to 42% of total revenue
EBITDA margin expansion from ~14.5% to ~18.5% through SG&A leverage and gross margin improvement
Growth capex in automation supporting operational efficiency
risks: Halverson family rollover dependency (~19%); founder transition risk
Revenue timing pull-forward from key OEM customer normalized out in QofE
Below-market facility lease at Ft. Lauderdale HQ requiring renegotiation at FMV
High leverage: $320M TLB on $56M EBITDA (~5.7x gross leverage)
Significant capex intensity ($28–32M annually in early hold period)
